missionPremise: The publish-gate scheduler graded 17 of the 65 closed parcel-record rails (SLATE_1+1B+1C+1D+LANDUSE_OWNER_GATE_GAP). Canon requires 'unaccounted' to be fatal at publish; for 48 of 65 rails that was unenforced. D5's ruling: widen DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS (publish-gate-sched.mjs) to derive from the closed rail set (rail-keys.js, PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS, 65), on the stated premise that grading is not serving and this is customer-invisible. That premise was TRUE for parcelRecordAllowlist.ts (legacy-design-tools, confirmed at source: parcelRecordAllowlist.ts:356-359, a slated pair with a non-pass verdict fails soft to legacy) and FALSE for this repo's own pre-bake publish gate (publish-readiness-gate.mjs, consumed with no override by bastrop-publish.mjs's live publish path -- fails hard, throws, refuses the bake). Full detail, evidence and file:line citations in CP1.
codeChange: DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS (src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs) now = Object.freeze([...PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS]), derived from rail-keys.js, never hand-authored, length 65 (test-pinned). The five slate constants (SLATE_1/1B/1C/1D, LANDUSE_OWNER_GATE_GAP) are unchanged; their union is preserved under a new name, SLATE_1_THROUGH_LANDUSE_OWNER_UNION, since DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS no longer means that union. Added PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS (src/lib/publish-readiness-gate.mjs): a deliberately separate, explicitly documented POLICY FLOOR (analogous to parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE -- a curated, hand-declared subset, not a denominator), seeded at the pre-D5 17-rail union, asserted at load time to be a subset of PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS, with its expansion path documented for later OPS-21 lanes. evaluatePreBakeReadiness and requirePreBakeReadiness now default `requiredRails` to PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS instead of DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS -- bastrop-publish.mjs (unmodified, still calls with no override) is therefore provably unaffected.
decisionAuthorization: The decoupling design (Option A, with three named refinements: name the floor as a policy subset not a frozen list; assert subset-of-65 at load time; document the expansion path so the floor is not a permanent carve-out) was an explicit operator/user ruling made mid-lane via AskUserQuestion on 2026-09-10, after this lane surfaced and evidenced the publish-readiness-gate hazard the dispatch's STANDING FACTS did not account for. The user also asked for precise reconciliation of an apparent contradiction (schoolDistrict already refusing in the live table vs. the dispatch's 'no customer impact' claim); resolved by reading parcelRecordAllowlist.ts at source (legacy-design-tools origin/main) -- both claims are true simultaneously because they describe two different gates on the same table with opposite failure semantics (fail-soft LDT serve routing vs. fail-hard Factory publish gate). Full narrative in CP1.

fleetMemoryScratch: LESSON: a shared constant used as both a grading denominator and a hard-fail publish-blocking floor is a landmine -- widening 'the graded set' silently widens 'what blocks the bake' unless the two are deliberately named and decoupled. Check every consumer of a constant a dispatch names before widening it, not just the one the dispatch describes.

LESSON: parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's serve-side gate and a repo's own pre-bake/publish gate can read the identical verdict table with opposite failure semantics (fail-soft vs fail-hard) -- a 'this is customer-invisible' claim about one is not evidence about the other.
